approach: Add a read-only, filtered commit view to the producer and verifier snapshots, only when the request text names commit hashes. A new `Snapshot::add_commit_views` resolves each named hash in the user's repository and keeps it only if it is an ancestor of the base commit. For each kept commit it writes the full hash, date, subject, visible changed paths and a unified diff limited to visible paths into one file, `ATHENA-COMMITS.txt`, at the snapshot root. Visibility uses the same `classify()` and `visible_to_agents()` filter as `history_text` and `materialize`. The diff is taken with a literal-pathspec list on stdin, so hidden paths never reach the output. No user object, ref, alternate or remote enters the snapshot: the core generates the text and the agent's git still holds only synthetic commits. The file is listed in the snapshot's `.git/info/exclude`, so `git add -A`, the change list, the candidate commit and the verifier's `prepared` tree ignore it. A new `commit_hashes_in(text)` extracts candidate hashes (7 to 40 hex characters, at least one digit and one letter, at most 8). `producer_snapshot` and `verifier_snapshot` call both with the request text. The brief text, D08, enforcement.md and the changelog are updated. With no hash in the request nothing is added, so snapshots are unchanged. Revision 2 drops docs/system-facts.md from the files (it is not a deliverable) and flags the stale line as a question. It also gives criterion 6 a seam and a fails_without. It says why the one-line edits to the other `verifier_snapshot` callers and the core test file cannot be avoided.

decisions.choice: Generate a filtered text view (ATHENA-COMMITS.txt) in the core; do not expose any real git objects inside the snapshot.
decisions.reason: Real objects in an alternates store, a fetched pack or a remote leak hidden-path blobs and trees through the object database, reachable with `git cat-file` or `git log --all`. A generated file reuses the existing classify()/visible_to_agents() filter as `history_text` does, and agents read it with Read and Grep, which every role already has. The user's repository is only read.

rejected.option: Alternates or a remote pointing at the user's repository
rejected.why: Gives a path back to the user's objects, including records/ and athena-exclude content. Criterion 3 forbids it, and so does D08's isolation.

rejected.option: Rewrite the named commits into the snapshot's own git (copy trees with hidden paths removed, then commit them)
rejected.why: Gives real `git show`, but the rewritten commits get new ids, so the hash the request cites would not resolve. It also needs tree surgery across merges, and one unfiltered mistake would put hidden blobs in the object store.

rejected.option: Always include full history, or extend HISTORY.txt
rejected.why: Out of scope: full history is not wanted for every agent, and the HISTORY.txt format must not change.

decisions.choice: Keep the view out of the commits and the work tree's tree by listing `/ATHENA-COMMITS.txt` in `.git/info/exclude`, written after the base and candidate commits exist. `copy_files` skips that name at the top level for a resumed directory.
decisions.reason: The producer's candidate and the verifier's `prepared` tree both come from `git add -A` (work_tree_tree, commit_all). Without the exclude the file would appear as an added file in the candidate, would break the verifier's `tree_now == prepared` check (verification.rs:299, 327), and would break the unchanged-snapshot invariant of criterion 4.

rejected.why: Ripgrep skips hidden directories by default, so Grep would not find it, and the brief would have to name an unusual path.

rejected.option: Commit the file into the snapshot's base commit
rejected.why: It would change the one-commit/two-commit shape and the base tree the change list is measured against.

decisions.choice: Accept a hash only if it resolves in the user's repository and is an ancestor of the base commit (`is_ancestor`). Everything else, including a commit that changed only hidden paths, is listed in the file under one shared note: `not available: not in the base commit's history, or changed only paths hidden from agents`. The result is Ok with the hash in `CommitViews.omitted`: no error and no panic.
decisions.reason: Records-branch and other unreachable commits are excluded by the ancestor rule. One shared note means the file does not confirm that a hidden commit exists. A typo in a quoted hash must not fail the job, and the agent is told why nothing is shown.

rejected.option: Refuse the job on an unknown hash
rejected.why: A mistyped or non-hash token would stop the job over a convenience feature.
The agent could not tell a missing view from an empty one, which is the fault behind the rejected attempts.

decisions.choice: Take hashes only from the request text (`ctx.job.request.text`) through a tokenizer: split on non-alphanumerics, keep tokens of 7 to 40 characters, all hex, with at least one digit and one letter, lowercase, deduplicated, at most 8.
decisions.reason: The reading says history is offered only for hashes the request names. The digit-and-letter rule drops the date part of job ids (20261012), plain numbers and all-hex words such as 'defaced'. Candidates are still checked by rev_parse, so a false positive costs only a note. A hash made only of digits is not detected; the changelog says so.

rejected.option: A regex crate over the whole brief
rejected.why: Adds a dependency and takes in hashes from plan text and other text the user did not write.

rejected.option: A new field on the request or config
rejected.why: Needs a record change, which this job rules out.

decisions.choice: One file, ATHENA-COMMITS.txt, at the snapshot root for both roles. It holds the subject only, not the commit body or author. Each commit's diff is cut at 200 KB with a visible truncation line.
decisions.reason: Mirrors HISTORY.txt (hash, date, subject, paths). A body can name hidden paths and an author is personal data (the `public` default).

rejected.why: More paths for the brief to explain and for in-tree name collisions; one file is enough for at most 8 commits.

decisions.choice: Change the signature of `verifier_snapshot` to take `ctx: &RunContext<'_>` instead of `pin_dir`, and edit the two callers outside verification.rs (mod.rs:1502, checks.rs:367) by one line each. Add the core wiring test to run_pin_tests.rs.
decisions.reason: `verifier_snapshot` has the base, the candidate and the pin dir but not the request text, and every caller already holds `ctx` (checked at verification.rs:298, 326, mod.rs:1502, checks.rs:367, all passing `ctx.pin_dir.as_deref()`). The two edits are mechanical and cannot be avoided without hidden state. run_pin_tests.rs holds the only fake-invoker harness that can drive a whole job and see the producer's and the verifier's workdirs, so criterion 4's core half needs it.

rejected.option: Keep the old signature and stash the requested hashes in a field on Athena or in a file
rejected.why: Adds shared state across runs that every caller would have to keep in step; the explicit argument is smaller and safer.

rejected.option: Skip the core wiring test and rely on athena-git tests only
rejected.why: The wiring in producer.rs and verification.rs would then have no behavior evidence, which the behavior-evidence default rejects.

decisions.choice: Do not edit docs/system-facts.md; raise its stale 'Producer snapshot ... history absent' line as a question for the user.
decisions.reason: It is not a listed deliverable and the brief says to keep the change focused. D08, enforcement.md, the changelog and the briefs carry the new rule.

rejected.why: Widens scope beyond the listed deliverables without the user's agreement.

risks.risk: A hidden path name or content leaks through the diff, for example from a rename, a submodule line, or a textconv or external diff driver set in the user's .gitattributes.
risks.mitigation: The path list comes from `diff_tree` with `--no-renames`, is filtered by `classify()`, and is passed as literal pathspecs. `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv` are set. Entries with mode 160000 are dropped. Commit body and author are never written. Criterion 2 checks the file bytes and every object in the snapshot.

risks.risk: The view file leaks into the candidate commit or changes the verifier's `prepared` tree, which would make a verdict discard itself and rerun.
risks.mitigation: The path goes into `.git/info/exclude` before the file is written; `git add -A` in `commit_all` and `work_tree_tree` respects it. Tests compare `work_tree_tree()` before and after and check the candidate's tree in the core test.

risks.risk: A real tracked file already named ATHENA-COMMITS.txt in the repository.
risks.mitigation: `add_commit_views` returns Refused if the base tree tracks that name rather than overwriting it. The core call turns that into a warning line and the job continues without the view.

risks.risk: Huge commits (generated files, vendored code) make the file very large for Read.
risks.mitigation: At most 8 commits and 200 KB of diff per commit, then a visible truncation line; the path list is always complete.

risks.risk: False or missed hash detection in the request text (digit-only hashes missed, odd tokens matched).
risks.mitigation: The matcher is conservative and deterministic, tested on dates, job ids, versions and all-hex words. Every candidate is verified with `rev_parse`. A miss leaves today's behavior. The limit is stated in the changelog.

risks.risk: The snapshot lock or the immutable attribute prevents writing the view.
risks.mitigation: The view is written during creation, before any lock, in both snapshot builders. The tests create and then lock a snapshot that holds the file.

risks.risk: docs/system-facts.md, read by the planner and critic, keeps saying history is absent from the producer snapshot, which is no longer fully true when a commit is named.
risks.mitigation: The line is left alone because it is outside the deliverables. It is raised as a question; D08, enforcement.md, the changelog and the briefs state the exception.

risks.risk: The core wiring test depends on a harness in run_pin_tests.rs that was only located by grep, not read in full.
risks.mitigation: Step 7 reads the harness before writing the test; if it cannot expose both workdirs, the test records them through the same fake invoker at the two snapshot builders.

demonstrations.method: Athena-git unit test `named_commit_is_readable_in_a_producer_snapshot` in snapshot.rs. Build the user repo with `user_repo()` plus a later commit that adds src/feature.rs and edits src/main.rs. Call `Snapshot::create(.., SnapshotRepo::Base)`, then `snap.add_commit_views(&git, &head, &head, &[short hash of the extra commit])`. Read `ATHENA-COMMITS.txt` from the snapshot dir and assert the subject, the date, the paths `src/feature.rs` and `src/main.rs`, and the diff lines (`+++ b/src/feature.rs`, an added source line). Assert `CommitViews.shown` holds the full hash. A second case takes the hash from `commit_hashes_in("two fix attempts on commit <hash> were rejected")`.
demonstrations.observes: The file exists and contains the subject, the visible paths and the diff of the requested commit.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `add_commit_views` (or with it writing nothing) the file is missing and the read fails. The test does not compile against the pre-change crate.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Snapshot::add_commit_views` (added by plan step 2) after `Snapshot::create` (exists, snapshot.rs:59). Fixture: real temporary git repositories from `testutil::repo_with` and `commit_all` (exist, lib.rs:1044 and 1062), injected as the `user: &Git` argument. No double; a real git runs.

demonstrations.method: Athena-git unit test `hidden_paths_never_appear_in_the_commit_view`. The requested commit changes src/main.rs (visible), FRONT.md (athena-exclude by the fixture's .gitattributes), private/notes.md (excluded by private/.gitattributes) and records/jobs/y.json, each hidden file holding a unique marker string. After `create` with `Base` and with `BaseAndCandidate`, plus `add_commit_views`, walk every file under the snapshot dir including `.git`. Because loose objects are zlib-compressed, also run `git log --all --stat -p` and `git cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch` inside the snapshot with `snap.git()`. Assert that no marker and no hidden path name (`FRONT.md`, `private/notes.md`, `records/jobs/y.json`, `records/`) appears in file bytes or git output. Also assert that HISTORY.txt from a `PlainWithHistory` snapshot of the same repo omits them. A second case: a requested commit that changed only hidden paths is listed under the 'not available' note and its subject is not in the file.
demonstrations.observes: No marker content and no hidden path name anywhere in the snapshot or its git output, while the visible part of the same commit is present, so the test is not vacuous.
demonstrations.fails_without: With a plain unfiltered `git show <hash>` as the diff, the markers and path names would appear in the file and the assertions would fail. The test first builds that unfiltered output in the user repo and asserts the markers are present there, which shows the content is reachable without the filter.

demonstrations.method: Athena-git unit test `unknown_or_unreachable_hashes_are_omitted_with_a_note`. Inputs: a well-formed hash that does not exist (`deadbeef12`), an abbreviation of a real commit on a side branch not reachable from the base commit, and a commit on an orphan `athena/records`-style branch. Assert `add_commit_views` returns Ok (no panic, no error), `CommitViews.omitted` holds all three, `shown` is empty, and `ATHENA-COMMITS.txt` exists with the 'not available' note and no diff. The doc comment states that the chosen behavior is omission with a note, not refusal. A further case with 9 distinct valid hashes asserts that only the first 8 are used and the file notes the rest are ignored.

demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `rev_parse` and `is_ancestor` guard, an unreachable commit's diff would be written (the side-branch case fails) and an unknown hash would surface a git error instead of Ok.
